text:
Predicates:
Bark(x) ::: x barks.
Dog(x) ::: x is a dog.
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
Jump(x) ::: x jumps.
HasLegs(x) ::: x has legs.
Terricolous(x) ::: x is terricolous.
KiKi ::: specific individual.
Likes(x, y) ::: x likes y.
Premises:
¬Likes(jane, y) if Bark(y) ::: Jane does not like any animals that bark.
∀x (Dog(x) → Bark(x)) ::: All dogs are animals that bark.
∀x (Animal(x) → Jump(x)) ::: All animals that jump.
∀x (HasLegs(x) → Jump(x)) ::: If an animal has legs, then it jumps.
∀x (Terricolous(x) → HasLegs(x)) ::: If an animal is terricolous, then it has legs.
Animal(KiKi) ::: KiKi is an animal.
(¬Jump(KiKi) ∧ ¬HasLegs(KiKi)) → (Terricolous(KiKi) ∨ HasLegs(KiKi)) ::: If KiKi neither jumps nor has legs, then KiKi is terricolous or has legs.
Conclusion:
¬Bark(KiKi) ∧ ¬Dog(KiKi) ::: KiKi does not bark and he is not a dog.
